summary: A BookTrust web page giving ten tips from Luisa Plaja, former editor of the teen fiction site Chicklish, on how to start a book blog. The tips cover naming the blog, choosing a platform, setting up About and Review Policy pages, adding posts from books already owned or borrowed, joining memes and reading challenges, writing list posts, linking favourite sites, and having fun.
one_line: Ten tips from former Chicklish editor Luisa Plaja on starting a book blog, from naming it to joining the online book community.
key_facts: Luisa Plaja is the former editor of Chicklish, a teen fiction site which ran from 2006 to 2014.
Chicklish got its name from its origins as a review site for romantic comedy books for teenagers, so 'a bit like chick lit'.
Two of the most popular free blogging platforms named in the note are Blogger and Wordpress.
Chicklish used Typepad as its blogging platform.
A blogger can name a book blog after themselves, for example 'Katie Reads'.
A 'Review Policy' page can outline whether a blogger accepts books for review and what genres and formats, such as e-books, will be considered.
New book bloggers are advised to build their blog first from books they have obtained themselves, such as books borrowed from the library.
The meme 'In My Mailbox' involves listing all the books received or borrowed in a given week.
The meme 'Waiting on Wednesday' involves writing about an upcoming release and posting it on a Wednesday.
List post ideas include five favourite reads this year, favourite characters, or book gift ideas, illustrated with book covers.
Goodreads is suggested for book information and cover images, and Fantastic Fiction for full series listings.
Favourite book sites should be listed in a sidebar, and the blogger should comment regularly on other sites.
The note's tenth and final tip is simply 'Have fun!'.
The article is part of BookTrust's Writing tips section, under Tips for young writers and Authors' tips for getting started.
